name: review-flight-deck
title: A reviewer surface above several pull requests
outcome: On every pull request change, the flightdeck offers several ways to review the currently open set. Each way carries a narrative and a diagram. The reviewer picks one, and the pick is recorded.
done_when: A pull request event starts the mode without a person naming a set.
The mode writes at least two competing proposals for the open set, and states the evidence under each.
Each proposal carries one short narrative and one diagram.
A proposal names what it could not assess, instead of leaving the gap silent.
The reviewer acts on a proposal step without leaving the page, and each action appends one ledger line.
The reviewer opens any pull request of the set in the existing four-level layout, and returns to the proposal.
The reviewer picks one proposal, and the ledger records the pick and the proposals that were refused.
The viewer renders the proposals and computes none of them.
abort_if: The stop count for a set is not materially lower than the total number of authored files the pull requests change. Measured over 27 pairs of merged pull requests in this bundle, the ratio runs from 0.00 to 0.41, and every pair reduces. This criterion is met for the whole corpus.

Superseded criterion, kept for the record: the first version of this test compared the stop count against the shared-file list, not against the total changed files. That was the wrong baseline, because a reviewer's alternative is reading both diffs in full, not reading the shared subset. On that wrong baseline only 9 of 27 pairs reduce, and pull requests 11 and 12 give 37 stops against 22 shared files.
A proposed partition anchors reviewers more than it helps them, measured against a set they also reviewed without one.

min_work.derived_from: 3 districts touched (viewer, scripts, .cobuilder-architect). 4 colliding ADRs: ADR-0001 (one self-contained file under a blocking content policy), ADR-0018 (one lifecycle surface and a derived record index), ADR-0019 (the append-only ledger, with its vocabulary fixed at comment, reply, and state), ADR-0020 (viewer parts and an author-time build, decided and not executed). 1 boundary rule crossed: no plugin names another plugin's path, so the viewer reaches the proposal through the bundle.
min_work.note: Stage 3 issued six isolated exploration frames and one separate critic pass. Stage 4 raised three challenges and the engineer answered all three. The engineer overruled the recommended approach and chose the Braid and the Cut together, on the ground that both do work on the reviewer's behalf before the reviewer arrives. That choice replaced the stated approach and moved the whole computation terminal-side, which also removed the ledger write-path defect the first challenge raised. Stage 7 asked whether this is one pull request or several. The engineer chose one, so every epic carries the same branch, design/review-flight-deck, and the six epics are units of work inside one review rather than six pull requests. A scratchpad run of E1's arithmetic over the cached diffs corrected the first abort criterion, which compared stops against shared files rather than against total changed files. Round 2: the engineer revised the intent. The mode is named flightdeck. It runs on a pull request event, not on a named set, and it offers several proposals rather than one partition. Each proposal carries a narrative and a diagram. The six epics collapse into four. ADR-0022's boundary holds unchanged. Automatic triggering collides with the no-hooks install rule and is the one open decision. Round 3: the engineer resolved the trigger themselves, with a scheduled skill run or a workflow, and it stops being an open question. The remaining work is the layout and the proposal quality. flightdeck-prototype.html is the layout, close to working: three views, the actions a reviewer takes from the page, a drill-in to the existing four-level layout, and an append-only ledger.

epics.outcome: The mode lists every open pull request with its head branch, its changed files, and its design.
epics.note: The same work as the first epic of the inflight-record-store design. Build it once, in shared code.

epics.outcome: The mode writes at least two competing proposals for the open set, each naming a review order, a reason, and its evidence.
epics.note: The only new work. divergent-exploration.md already generates competing options and criticises them in a separate pass. The region walk moves inside this epic as evidence, and stops being a reviewer-facing step.

epics.outcome: Each proposal carries one narrative and one Mermaid diagram of how the pull requests read together.
epics.note: story-mode and mermaid already cover this. build_diagrams.py keys on a pull request number, so it needs a proposal key.

epics.outcome: The viewer renders the proposals, the reviewer acts on a step from the page, and each action appends one ledger line. A step can open a pull request in the existing four-level layout and return.
epics.note: Reuses the existing view modes, the level rail, and the ledger from ADR-0019. flightdeck-prototype.html is the reference layout for this epic.
